summary.intent: Run the full GSD phase pipeline for phase 69 (FUSE/WinFsp Rust port with grant-root awareness): plan the phase end-to-end (research → validation → pattern-mapping → planning → verification → coverage gates), then auto-advance into wave-based parallel execution.
summary.outcome: Phase 69 planning completed (14 plans across 7 waves, committed at `23b4ba198`) after recovering from a planner crash mid-run (missing 69-14 written via a fresh single-plan planner, TEST-03 frontmatter gap fixed). Execution then began: pre-flight gates passed, a synchronous canary (69-01) validated the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline, and Waves 1–2 (5/14 plans) completed and merged cleanly with all cargo checks and tests green; Wave 3 setup was in progress when the transcript ends.

repo: GSD commit helper in this repo has a known false-negative: it reports `commit_failed` even when `git log` shows the commit landed cleanly (lint-staged completes fine) — always verify via `git log` rather than trusting the reported status.

The API-SURFACE.md intel hook regen is TS/JS-focused and returns `symbolCount: 0, stale: true` for Rust-only phases — expected, safe to omit from planner prompts when RESEARCH.md already has verified symbol locations.

gsd-planner can crash mid-run on an API error (connection closed) after writing several plans to disk uncommitted; recovery is to diff what's actually on disk vs. what was referenced in the partial summary, then spawn a fresh single-plan planner for just the missing plan rather than restarting the whole planning run.

Plan `requirements:` frontmatter can drift from the phase's real requirement ID — the planner used internal pseudo-IDs (SC-01..SC-06) instead of the actual roadmap requirement `TEST-03`; the §13 coverage gate checks the real ID, so this must be caught and fixed on the plan carrying that scope item.

Fresh git worktrees created for executor agents may lack `node_modules`, causing the husky pre-commit hook to fail (`lint-staged` not found) on first commit — fix by running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the worktree before retrying.

`cipher-box-phase69` is itself a linked git worktree of the `cipher-box` repo, so nested executor worktrees resolve under `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/`, not under the phase69 directory — the orchestrator must pin `orchestrator_root` correctly in the manifest for this case.

The desktop E2E GitHub Actions workflow's actual name is "Desktop E2E Tests", not "CI E2E Tests" as the ROADMAP/CONTEXT docs word it — using the wrong name in `gh workflow run` would 404; this was caught by the 69-14 planner and corrected in that plan.

`GET /shares/sent` (`SentShareResponseDto`) has no `revoked`/status field because shares are hard-deleted on revoke — every row returned is inherently an active grant, confirmed against the live DTO source (`apps/api/src/shares/dto/share-response.dto.ts`).

Literal-string truth-checks in plans (e.g. `grep -n 'ecies'`) can false-positive on innocuous doc-comment substrings like `ecies::unwrap_key` used only to explain what code replaces — reword the comment rather than treating it as a real deviation.

code.finding: RotationHighWater<S: HighWaterStore> ports ROT-07 durable anti-rollback gate from packages/sdk/src/state/rotation-high-water.ts with fail-closed enforce_resolved matching exact TS ordering (validate live input → generation-floor → cold-device-versionFloor-or-warm-seq-floor → bump both monotonic-max).
JsonSidecarFloorStore implements HighWaterStore via an atomic JSON sidecar write (temp file + rename, 0600 perms via OpenOptionsExt) with no new storage dependency (no sled/redb/rusqlite).
AAD-bound seal_node/unseal_node implemented symmetrically (no ECIES) for node-to-node hops, per SC#1 primitive.

has_covering_grant/maybe_rotate_on_scope_exit ported from TS packages/sdk-core/src/rotation/scope.ts as the single grant-scope predicate (Pitfall 1 in plan-checker); includes SC#4/ROT-02 zero-rotation invariant and T-63-17 anti-malicious-relay cross-check tests.
list_sent_shares/collect_sent_shares wrapper for GET /shares/sent; documented finding that response DTO has no revoked/status field since shares are hard-deleted on revoke.

workflow: When a subagent (planner) crashes mid-run, verify actual filesystem state (frontmatter validity, completeness, requirement coverage) before deciding whether to resume or restart — resuming with a narrowly-scoped fresh agent (single-plan mode) preserves role separation and avoids re-doing completed work.
For long unattended multi-hour operations, writing a durable handoff file to a scratchpad path before pausing/scheduling a wakeup protects against context summarization losing recovery state.

Before fanning out multiple parallel worktree-isolated executor agents on a risky/interdependent phase, run one plan synchronously as a canary to validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo-gate pipeline before committing to full parallelism.

Detect intra-wave file conflicts (two plans editing the same file, e.g. crates/sdk/src/lib.rs) ahead of dispatch and serialize just those plans while keeping the rest of the wave parallel, rather than serializing the whole wave.
Executor subagents intentionally do not modify STATE.md/ROADMAP.md in worktree mode — that's reserved for the orchestrator after merge, per the worktree-mode contract.

friction: gsd-planner hit an API error (connection closed) mid-response while writing the 7th/final plan (69-14), losing the live agent context (though prior plans were already persisted to disk), requiring a multi-step manual recovery.

Plan-checker flagged that requirements frontmatter used internal pseudo-IDs (SC-01..SC-06) instead of the real requirement ID TEST-03, which would have silently failed the §13 coverage gate if not caught.
GSD's commit helper repeatedly reports false-negative `commit_failed` status even when commits land cleanly, requiring manual `git log` verification after every commit step.
Fresh worktrees lack node_modules, breaking husky pre-commit hooks on first commit in each new worktree-isolated executor agent, requiring an ad hoc `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` fix each time.
A doc-comment substring match false-triggered a plan's literal grep truth-check for absence of ECIES usage, requiring investigation to confirm it was a false positive.
